title: TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary transmits images of armed poachers on two dates; Dudhwa Tiger Reserve officials identify them and investigate
summary: A TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary sent officials images of poachers with a gun and knives on two dates in 2022; officials identified them, and later sources claim arrests.
account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. The paper states that the seven Dudhwa units ran from early September 2022 to mid-December 2022. All seven transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. The paper does not give the dates of the detections, so the two poacher detections can be placed only within the deployment period. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar and RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, as saying that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment as saying that poachers caught on camera had helped forest authorities secure a conviction a year later. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer: “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. Agence France-Presse (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found. A Clemson University release of 6 August 2025 states that TrailGuard AI has contributed to the arrests of more than 20 poachers, but it names no reserve or case.
purpose: Built to detect tigers and people on trails with embedded AI and send real-time images to forest officials. Detecting and transmitting the poachers' images was that purpose.
system: TrailGuard AI camera-alert system (embedded AI on an Intel computer-vision chip; cellular transmission)
developer: Nightjar / RESOLVE, Washington DC (inventor Steve Gulick), with CVEDIA Ltd
deployer: Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh Forest Department, with the Global Tiger Forum, National Tiger Conservation Authority and Clemson University
location: Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh, India
taxonomy_note: The paper documents detection and identification of armed poachers for investigation, with arrests claimed only in releases, and the protected asset is wildlife.

ratings.reason: Forest officials received the images in near real time and identified the individuals. The paper documents an investigation, not an arrest or prosecution, so the recorded gain is an investigative lead.

Protection of the reserve's wildlife from this gang is claimed through arrests only in the Clemson release, developer material and The Hindu's second-hand report. The paper notes a chital presumably poached before the second detection.

ai_role.statement: The camera's on-board classifier filtered motion triggers to people and tigers and transmitted the poachers' images to officials' phones within about a minute. Identification and investigation were done by officials. The peer-reviewed account is co-authored by the developers (RESOLVE, CVEDIA) with Dudhwa and Wildlife Institute of India staff and stops at “investigating”. The arrest claim rests on a Clemson release quoting the ex-field director, developer press releases and The Hindu quoting the manufacturer and an unnamed participant.

ratings.reason: Forest officials received the images in near real time and identified the individuals. The paper documents an investigation, not an arrest or prosecution, so the recorded gain is an investigative lead.

Protection of the reserve's wildlife from this gang is claimed through arrests only in the Clemson release, developer material and The Hindu's second-hand report. The paper notes a chital presumably poached before the second detection.

display.answer: The peer-reviewed paper is co-authored by the system's developers and Dudhwa staff, and Agence France-Presse relays its claim. The paper reports identification and an investigation but no arrest. The Clemson release carries Nightjar and RESOLVE boilerplate, and The Hindu quotes the manufacturer and an unnamed participant. The arrest claims therefore trace back to people involved in the project.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: A TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary sent officials images of poachers with a gun and knives on two dates in 2022; officials identified them, and later sources claim arrests.
fields.account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. The paper states that the seven Dudhwa units ran from early September 2022 to mid-December 2022. All seven transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. The paper does not give the dates of the detections, so the two poacher detections can be placed only within the deployment period. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar and RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, as saying that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment as saying that poachers caught on camera had helped forest authorities secure a conviction a year later. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer: “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. Agence France-Presse (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found. A Clemson University release of 6 August 2025 states that TrailGuard AI has contributed to the arrests of more than 20 poachers, but it names no reserve or case.
